## Where code goes

These architectures are in force. Code that breaks them fails `smith lint`.

- `vertical-slices`: code grouped by what it does.

One folder is one slice: one outcome, flat, with no sub-folders. Put new code in the slice it belongs to, or make a new slice. Do not make a folder named `common`, `data`, `helper`, `manager`, `misc`, `processor`, `shared`, `util` (or their plurals).

## Naming and file roles

A file is named for the role it plays. The roles are `handler`, `use_case`, `algorithm`, `policy`, `model`, `contract`, `mapper`, `validator`, `repository`, `client`, `store`, `middleware`, `error`, `config`, `enum`.

- go: `<name>_<role>.go`, tests `<name>_<role>_test.go`.
- node: `<name>.<role>.ts` with the role in kebab-case (`place-order.use-case.ts`), checked by the ESLint config.

Run `smith slices check` to check the names.

## Add a project

Create a project with smith. Do not copy a folder by hand.

```sh
smith add <app|lib|package> <name> --lang <language>
smith add app web --lang node --with react,vitest
```

`smith kinds` lists the kinds, `smith choices` lists the choices for `--with`, and `smith stacks` lists the stacks. A project follows what its sibling projects already do.

## Done means

Run these before you say a change is done.

```sh
smith lint
smith test
smith build
smith doctor
smith derive --check
smith ci verify
```

`smith ci verify` is the same check as CI. A change is done when it passes.
Commits use Conventional Commits: a merge to `main` releases what they describe.

## Derived files: do not edit by hand

smith writes these files from facts and the project graph. A hand edit is reported as drift and never kept silently. Change the input, then run `smith derive`.

- `apps/web/tsconfig.lib.json`

To own one of them, run `smith derive --eject <file>`. `smith why <file>` says who owns any file and why.

These were ejected and are yours to edit:

- `apps/web/jest.config.js`

## Projects and their choices

| Project | Folder | Kind | Language | Stack | Choices |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| api | `apps/api` | app | go | go | none |
| web | `apps/web` | app | node | react-vitest | react, vitest |

`smith explain <project>` shows how its tasks resolved.
